body: Regular cars in Qatar have long, white licence plates with a maroon strip on the left. Trucks have square, black licence plates, and police plates are blue.
The Google car is often a blurred white pickup truck with a visible antenna on the left. Sometimes, rusty clips can be seen on the crossbar.
Qatar's landscape is a predominantly arid and mostly flat desert. You will not see a lot of trees or other greenery.
Qatar typically uses solid outer white lines with either white or yellow in the middle. Less commonly, you can find outer yellow lines.
Qatar uses round poles with 3 insulators on the pole top, where the middle one is slightly higher. The crossbar is connected to the pole with 2 diagonal bars.
Qatar uses white on red and white on blue chevrons.
Since some coverage was taken before the 2022 World Cup, you may see many banners mentioning the event.
Qatari crossing signs are unique for featuring a man in a thobe.
Qatar is well-covered by Street View, with most main roads and some side roads included. The south and west of the country currently lack coverage.
Qatar is divided into municipalities, which are further divided into numbered zones. These numbers can be seen on street signs and used to identify your location.
A very short antenna on the Google car is a good clue for being in northern Qatar.
A fairly long antenna on the Google car is primarily found in and around Doha.
This long antenna on the Google car is mostly found in southwestern Qatar.
Bollards in Qatar are found on only a few specific roads. For example, one road has black and yellow center lines, while another is coastal with many shrubs.
Al Bayt Stadium can be recognized by the black and white horizontal stripes on its exterior and its tent-like roof.
Lusail Stadium, located in Lusail, is recognizable by its golden bowl-like shape.
Four towers in Lusail, resembling a screw thread, are visible from almost every point in the city.
A structure resembling a gahfiya (a traditional cap) can be seen around the Ahmed bin Ali Stadium.
The Mall of Qatar has a boxy appearance with many ads on the side and is next to large car parks.
Education City Stadium is recognizable by its large, grey cladding with a diamond pattern.
Education City features distinctive black-tiled roads.
Brown street signs, often fixed low to the ground, are a feature of Education City.
Khalifa International Stadium is recognizable by its dual arches that look like a wide-open mouth.
The Torch Tower, Qatar's tallest building, can be seen from most of the Baaya District and has a distinct hyperboloid structure.
A cardboard box in the right side of the truck bed, along with rusty clips, is a clue for Lusail. This may not always be visible.
A black box on the left side of the truck bed can be seen southeast of Ar-Rayyan. This clue may not always be present.
The black box on the right side of the truck bed is seen in Al Khor and near the Torch Tower. This may not always be visible.
Tripod coverage was used to capture the interior of Hamad International Airport, including unique coverage from inside an airplane.
